content: {"summary":"Both notification-worker pods saw DNS lookups stall for seconds and some returned getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN. The cluster default ndots:5 made each short name generate eight UDP queries, increasing the chance of lost replies. A lost reply triggers a 5‑second timeout and retry, adding latency; losing both attempts produces EAI_AGAIN.","likely_cause":"Cluster default ndots:5 causing many DNS queries per short name, leading to UDP reply loss, timeouts, retries and occasional EAI_AGAIN errors.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Both notification-worker pods experienced slow DNS lookups, with some returning getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN.","evidence_ids":["INC-0179#0","RB-021#7"],"quote":"Both workers resolved names slowly, and a few lookups finished in `EAI_AGAIN`"},{"text":"The cluster default ndots:5 caused each short name lookup to generate eight UDP queries, increasing chance of lost replies.","evidence_ids":["RB-021#4"],"quote":"One lookup is 4 names × 2 record types = 8 queries over UDP"},{"text":"When a DNS reply is lost, the resolver waits the 5‑second timeout and retries, adding ~5 s latency.","evidence_ids":["RB-021#4"],"quote":"resolver waits out its 5 s timeout and asks that query again"},{"text":"If both attempts of a query are lost, getaddrinfo returns EAI_AGAIN, causing occasional failures.","evidence_ids":["RB-021#5"],"quote":"getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN needs both tries of one query lost"}],"next_checks":["Verify the ndots setting in the notification-worker pods’ /etc/resolv.conf","Monitor DNS UDP reply loss rates during peak bursts","Consider lowering ndots or increasing UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE to mitigate thread contention","Check for any recent changes to dnsConfig or pod deployments affecting ndots"]}
